sections.h2: Where is the Lapeer County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office serves all of Lapeer County and is open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. The office page has a Location Directions link for the street address. Its stated aim is to administer Michigan statutes as they apply to the office and to process documents that follow the Michigan Recording Act promptly.

Anything that conveys or encumbers Lapeer County land goes through this office: deeds, mortgages, discharges and similar instruments. Checks are made payable to Lapeer County Register of Deeds, and the office takes cash, checks, money orders and, inside the office, credit cards. Title companies and attorneys are asked to send electronic recordings through Simplifile, which has its own support line at 800.460.5657.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Lapeer County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed costs $30 per document, however many pages it has, and a sale adds transfer tax and sometimes a tax certificate. The county's published schedule lists each charge.

sections.h2: Which Lapeer County deeds need a tax certificate first?
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, land contracts, assignments of land contracts and any deed that includes a covenant of warranty need a certificate from the County Treasurer before the Register of Deeds will take them.

The certificate costs $5 and comes from the County Treasurer, so plan that stop before you carry the deed to the recording counter. The schedule names warranty deeds, land contracts, land contract assignments and deeds with a covenant of warranty. If you are recording a different instrument, ask the treasurer's office whether it needs one. When the parcel has back taxes, ask the treasurer what must be paid before a certificate is issued.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax will a Lapeer County seller pay?
sections.html:
Add the two per thousand rates and apply them to the sale price: $8.60 per $1,000 in total. On a $250,000 house the county share is $275 and the state share is $1,875, for $2,150.

The tax falls on the seller, and the deed must state the total value of the real property or carry an affidavit declaring it. Under MCL 207.504 the county rate is 55 cents for each $500 or fraction, which matches the $1.10 per thousand on the local schedule. The county's Transfer Tax page links both the county and state exemption lists. Among the exemptions in MCL 207.505 are:

  • instruments where the value of the consideration is under $100;
  • instruments given as security, and their assignment or discharge;
  • leases, and land contracts under which title has not yet passed;
  • conveyances between spouses that create or end a tenancy by the entireties;
  • quitclaim deeds that only correct a flaw in a title already vested;
  • court orders that transfer property without a stated money consideration.

sections.h2: What does a Michigan deed need to be accepted for recording?
sections.html:
A deed must meet the page, signature and information rules in MCL 565.201 before a register of deeds may receive it. For instruments signed after April 1, 1997, each page needs a margin of at least 2.5 inches at the top of the first page and half an inch on the other sides.

  • The first line of print on page one must state the single recordable event the paper shows.
  • Print must be 10-point or larger, in black ink on white paper of at least 20-pound weight.
  • Pages must be no smaller than 8.5 by 11 inches and no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches, and attachments must meet the same size limits.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number must be obscured or removed.
  • A document in another language needs an attached English translation.
  • Instruments signed after January 1, 1964 carry the drafter's name and business address.

Once a document is recorded, the statute treats it as conforming, and the register may not turn away a compliant paper because of what it says.

sections.h2: What other fees can a Michigan register of deeds charge?
sections.html:
State law allows a few charges beyond recording, and the Lapeer schedule does not list all of them. MCL 600.2567 sets a fee of 50 cents for each year searched in a grantor and grantee search, with a $5 minimum, and $1 for filing or searching for any other paper.

  • Of the $30 recording fee, $5 goes into the county's automation fund.
  • A page means one side of a sheet at least 8.5 by 11 inches and not over 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Tax foreclosure deeds and forfeiture certificates recorded for a county treasurer can be billed within 30 days instead of at the counter.
  • Certifying a recorded document is $5, and plain copies are $1 a page.

Ask the office before you come in whether a search request would be charged under the statute.

sections.h2: How do I guard against deed fraud in Lapeer County?
sections.html:
Sign up for the free email fraud alert the office offers. It sends a message when any document is recorded under the name you register, so a forged deed or loan against your house shows up quickly.

The index page promotes the signup at the top, and a one page sign-up sheet is posted on the county site. Owners who plan to sell should also check that the name on the title matches the name they will sign with, since a mismatch between the printed name and the acknowledgment is one of the statutory reasons a deed is refused.

sections.h2: What is Lapeer County like for sellers?
sections.html:
Lapeer County is one of the five counties on the Thumb peninsula, and it is more rural than neighboring Oakland County. It covers 663 square miles, 20 of them water, and the Flint River starts at Columbiaville and runs toward Genesee County.

  • I-69 crosses the county east and west, and M-24 runs north and south through the City of Lapeer.
  • M-53 serves Imlay City, and M-90 passes through North Branch.
  • Neighbors are Sanilac, Tuscola, St. Clair, Genesee, Macomb and Oakland counties.

The population grew from 52,317 in 1970 to 70,038 in 1980 and 87,904 in 2000. The 2020 census counted 88,619, and a 2025 estimate put it near 89,516.

faqs.q: How much does the Lapeer County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $30 per document, no matter how many pages. A warranty deed also needs a $5 tax certificate from the County Treasurer, and the seller pays transfer tax of $1.10 plus $7.50 per $1,000 of value.

faqs.q: What are the Lapeer County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. The Location Directions link on the office page gives the street address.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Lapeer County Register of Deeds by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, inside the office. The schedule also lists cash, checks and money orders, with checks payable to Lapeer County Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Lapeer County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. The deed has to show the total value or have a valuation affidavit attached, and exemptions are listed in MCL 207.505 for the county tax.

faqs.q: Does Lapeer County offer a way to watch for fraudulent deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The office runs a free email alert that notifies you when a document is recorded under a name you enter.
